paper_metadata.title: Power Law Amplitude Estimation for Option Pricing with NISQ Devices

summary: The paper proposes a power-law amplitude estimation algorithm for European call option pricing and simulates it on Qiskit using 3 qubits: 2 qubits load a discretized log-normal asset-price distribution and 1 ancilla encodes payoff. The main quantitative claims are a theoretical oracle complexity of O(epsilon^-1) versus classical Monte Carlo O(epsilon^-2), and an empirical 13.12% accuracy improvement over QFT-free AE at k = 9.

experiments.description: Power-law amplitude estimation for pricing a European call option using a 3-qubit Qiskit simulation with a 2-qubit log-normal asset-price loader and 1 payoff ancilla, compared against QFT-free AE across several scheduling parameters k.

algorithm.variant: power law amplitude estimation (power-law AE) for option pricing

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Two qubits encode four discretized future asset prices; amplitudes represent the log-normal probability distribution. A third qubit encodes the option payoff via controlled Ry rotations.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate the expected payoff E[max(0, V-K)] for a European call option and recover option value from the measured ancilla probability P_pl.

problem_instance.description: European call option pricing under a Black-Scholes-Merton log-normal asset-price model.

dataset_specification.description: Possible expiration prices discretized to [3.981, 6.001, 8.022, 10.042] with probabilities [0.1%, 55.9%, 42.0%, 2.0%].

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Asset-price distribution truncated to an interval by three standard deviations; log-normal distribution parameters set from BSM model with T=30/365, volatility 50%, risk-free rate 2%, spot price 7.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Simulated in Qiskit; compared estimated option values for k in {3,5,7,9} against the analytical Black-Scholes-Merton value; reported overall accuracy improvement of about 13.12% over QFT-free AE.

implementation_details.classical_solver: maximum likelihood estimation for Bayesian update/post-processing
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Load discretized log-normal asset distribution; construct payoff via controlled Ry rotations and comparison circuit.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Maximum likelihood estimation over measurement outcomes to estimate theta_pl and recover option value from P_pl.

speedup_claims.conditions: amplitude estimation / amplitude amplification setting; option pricing via expected payoff estimation
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states the quadratic speedup in general AE context; the numerical experiment is a Qiskit simulation, not a hardware demonstration.

speedup_claims.conditions: from Fisher-information analysis for power-law AE; target error epsilon
speedup_claims.caveats: This is an asymptotic complexity claim derived analytically, not an empirical runtime measurement.

speedup_claims.conditions: European call option simulation at k = 9
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports the improvement qualitatively/numerically but does not provide the underlying absolute error values in text.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(epsilon^-1) oracle calls (from Fisher-information analysis for power-law AE; lower-bound error scales as O(N_q^-1))
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Monte Carlo methods require O(epsilon^-2) samples for comparable accuracy (stated as classical baseline context)

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: No hardware demonstration; only a 3-qubit Qiskit simulation with constant-shot Bayesian post-processing
limiting_factors: Only simulated results are reported, not a QPU run
Speedup is quadratic (O(epsilon^-1) vs classical Monte Carlo O(epsilon^-2)), which Hoefler-style constant-factor analysis generally deems insufficient for practical advantage
The circuit still requires state preparation/loading of a log-normal distribution and controlled rotations for payoff encoding
No end-to-end runtime or wall-clock comparison against classical methods is provided
The reported 13.12% improvement is only relative to QFT-free AE, not to a classical baseline

notes: Hardware inferred as simulator_other because the paper states the circuits were simulated on Qiskit and does not name a real QPU.
Circuit depth is not explicitly quantified; only qualitative statements about shallower circuits and reduced control gates are given.
The paper compares against QFT-free AE and classical Monte Carlo conceptually, but the reported numerical experiment is the Qiskit simulation of the power-law AE circuit for European call options.
The paper claims theoretical quadratic acceleration and reports a 13.12% accuracy improvement over QFT-free AE, but does not demonstrate practical quantum advantage over classical methods.
